benchmarks.name: Rick's Free Auto Repair Advice
benchmarks.note: PARTS ONLY, not a total: a named mechanic's guide (Rick Muscoplat, copyright 2017) prices one muffler for a 2015 Subaru Forester at $126.79 online, about $300 for a Walker muffler at a shop's price, and $368.57 for the genuine Subaru part, with a Subaru labor guide time of 0.6 hours per muffler. The article gives no total

finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so there is nothing to call too wide or too narrow; this file is a first build. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Toyota Corolla about $252-$642; midsize 2008 Toyota RAV4 2.4L about $169-$497; truck 2015 Ram 1500 5.7L about $226-$1,152; luxury 2012 Lexus ES 350 about $252-$821 for one of its two rear mufflers. So about $170-$1,150 covers the four examples, and the part is most of every total: the labor is roughly $60 to $320. How solid the labor times are: only the truck has a time for the example vehicle, and that one is a parts seller's 2-hour figure written for an owner fitting a bolt-on muffler at home. Every other range end is a maker-stated time for a different vehicle: Hyundai's 0.5 hour for the centre muffler on the 2014-2015 Tucson and FCA's 0.9 hour for the muffler on the 2015 Ram 2500 and 3500 5.7L. No maker-stated time for the Corolla, RAV4 rear muffler or ES 350 was found. Three figures support the 0.5-0.9 hour range without being used as ends: a Subaru book time of 0.6 hours per muffler for a 2015 Forester quoted by a named mechanic, Mazda's 0.4 hour for the 2019 CX-5 Turbo and Toyota's 1.0 hour for the centre muffler pipe on the 2006-2008 RAV4 V6 (the last two include an inspection, so they are cross-checks). All of these are times for bolted joints that come apart; a rusted flange or seized bolts on an older car add time, and the 0.9 hour top does not allow for that. Parts cautions: the Corolla low was seen on a retailer's 2018 Corolla page and the page does not confirm it fits a 2015 car; the RAV4 genuine prices are listed against both engines without saying which part fits which, so the top listed price is used; the Ram low is a bare Walker muffler whose page does not say direct fit, so it may need clamps or a weld; the ES 350 low is a store price that varies by location. On the RAV4, and on many other vehicles, the larger main muffler is part of a centre pipe that costs far more from the maker (genuine $1,683-$2,052 on the RAV4) and is outside this unit; a quote for 'a muffler' on such a vehicle may be for that part. Benchmarks: RepairPal's national average is $1,138-$1,190 with parts at about $1,035, far above the built totals, while its Corolla figure ($625-$661) sits at the top of the built economy range and its Silverado and F-150 figures ($706-$830) sit inside the built truck range. The national figure appears to price a dearer genuine part or a larger exhaust section; the page does not say which, so that is a reading, not a finding. Only RepairPal could be loaded as a full-cost benchmark (the third entry is parts only), short of the three independent estimates asked for. Confidence is low because three of the four classes have no labor time for the example vehicle and several parts prices have fitment gaps. This is an estimate, not a quote and not a diagnosis. Held (2026-11-20, first attempt, reviewer): three of the four low parts prices are not confirmed for the example vehicle (the Corolla price was read on a 2018 page with no part number, the Ram price is a bare muffler not stated to be direct fit, the Lexus price is a "from" price with no model years), the RAV4 main muffler is part of a center pipe outside this unit, and only the truck has a labor time for the example vehicle.
extras: A quote often adds new gaskets, clamps, bolts and rubber hangers, and labor to cut or heat rusted fasteners. Many shops recommend replacing the connecting pipe or resonator at the same time, and on cars with two rear mufflers the second one. If no bolt-on part is used, a muffler shop may cut the old one out and weld in a universal muffler, which is priced differently from this estimate. Also possible: a diagnosis or exhaust leak check fee, shop supplies and sales tax. A muffler replaced under a recall, service campaign or warranty extension is done by the dealer at no charge, so check for open campaigns first. An exhaust leak ahead of the muffler can let fumes into the cabin and should be looked at promptly; a noisy muffler alone is usually not an emergency.
